On This Day — August 31, 1945 A version of journalist Leslie Nakashima’s eyewitness report from Hiroshima ran in The New York Times, one of the first accounts of the atomic bomb’s devastation to reach American readers, and one of the first to be publicly contradicted by the same paper that printed it. Nakashima was born in Hawaii and had spent the war years in Tokyo as a correspondent for United Press. When Japan surrendered, he boarded a train to find his mother, who lived on the outskirts of Hiroshima. Sixteen days after the bomb fell, he arrived to find the city’s station in ruins, with nothing left standing between him and the mountains in the distance. His mother survived. The city she lived near did not. In his dispatch, Nakashima wrote plainly that what had been a city of 300,000 population had vanished, and estimated the death toll would reach 100,000.
